expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: `Subscription = Core & (| { readonly status: "trialing"; readonly trialEndsAt: Date } | { readonly status: "active"; readonly renewsAt: Date } | ...)`; four inline variants with status literals

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Canceled variant carries {status, canceledAt, cancellation}; Trialing carries {status, trialEndsAt}; intersection distributes so no variant contains optionals from others

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: `function assertNever(x: never)` defined; used in `accessEndsAt()` switch with four cases plus default; notes 'adding "paused" breaks the build here'

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId as `Brand<string, ...>`; RetryCount as `Brand<number, ...>` with range-checked constructor

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Single `transition(s: Subscription, e: Event): Subscription | TransitionError` function (shown as TODO stub); all fields readonly; 'The ONLY path to a new state. Every field is readonly so nothing else can assign one.'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists 6 numbered misuses: '(1) A single flat record...has 5 optionals — it claims 32 states are legal when 4 are', '(2) `voluntary: boolean` next to a free-text reason permits...', etc.; explains how each is prevented

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union; flat optional-fields record listed as first misuse and its problems detailed
